But the document head is still hardcoded (`<title>Pathland</title>`, generic viewport), and there is no meta/OG/structured data — so initial views lack rich SEO metadata.

**Goal:**
Make the server-rendered document fully crawlable and richly indexed without changing the protocol's declarative model.

- [x] Emit semantic landmarks (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<header>`/`<footer>`) and a real heading hierarchy from role/heading properties — **done**: semantic-only `ROLE` catalog + `TEXT_STYLE`-driven headings; landmark/heading conformance across Rust SSR + TS DOM client.

- [ ] Add SEO render tests (title/meta/landmark assertions) to both HTML renderers. Landmark assertions already exist in the conformance harness; title/meta assertions will follow with the meta feature.

**Technical Notes / Suggested Approach:**
Extend the `render(root)` API to accept document metadata; keep it a pure function of the opcode stream + metadata (no renderer state). # pathland-html-golden — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

Cross-renderer **golden conformance fixtures** for the HTML renderers.

## Implemented

- A battery of self-contained `PLPL` scenario batches (counter, form,
  composite controls, layout, tokens, **semantics** — semantic roles mapping to
  native elements/ARIA, **icons** — the `ICON` primitive's inline filled (Remix)
  SVG markup carrying `data-pathland-icon` (decorative + labeled, `FONT_SIZE`
  sizing), **sizethatfits** — the `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot with its selected
  child + `FIT_QUERY` LIST mirrored to `data-pathland-fit`, **media** —
  image alt/content-mode + a `VIDEO` surface bound to its `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`
  (non-visual hidden controller shell), **native_controls** — picker/date/color/
  progress/video native shells carrying their design-system classes,
  **framebounds** — a fill-width frame clamped by `MAX_WIDTH` around a fit slot
  (the player-bar first-paint regression), and a base→delta pair whose change
  includes a `ROLE` change exercising the semantic-tag retag), each rendered by
  the canonical Rust SSR renderer into committed fixtures under
  `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html`
  canonical `render_fragment`).
- `--emit` (regenerate fixtures) / `--check` (verify) CLI.
- `tests/guard.rs`: `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` fails if the committed
  fixtures no longer match the current renderer output.
- The TypeScript DOM client consumes the same fixtures in
  `lib/typescript/test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta),
  so the Rust SSR output is the single contract both renderers must reproduce.

## Regenerate

`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit` (or `npm run regen` from
`lib/typescript`), then commit the fixtures with the change that produced them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Scenario coverage is a representative slice (the core shells + tokens); it is
  not exhaustive over every property/component combination.

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
  `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
  `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
  self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
  former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
- **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
  committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
  fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
  client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
- **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
  surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
  size-that-fits snapshots.
- **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
  the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
  default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
  `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
  with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
- **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
  canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
  so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
- **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
  `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
  external/webfont requests.
- The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
  truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
  and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

# Plan: Issue #45 — SEO-hardened SSR

## Decisions (from your answers)

- **Protocol stays unchanged.** Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are renderer/host concerns (spec/OPCODE.md:534-536). Title, description, and locale continue to come from `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`.
- **App-driven per-route metadata** is required, so the app can define metadata from the active route before the first SSR paint.
- Structured data: **WebPage + Article** (Article derived from `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
- Starters emit SEO head by default, configurable via `pathland.seo.*`.
- Rust C ABI gets a flat meta struct for non-JVM hosts.

## Current state

- Head is built in exactly two places:
  - Rust: `render_document_with_head` at `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:1391`
  - Java: `renderDocument` at `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/HtmlRenderer.java:364`
- Both already map `TITLE` → `<title>`, `DESCRIPTION` → meta description, `LOCALE` → `<html lang>`.
- Semantic landmarks/headings are done.
- No canonical, OG, Twitter, or JSON-LD anywhere.
- SSR flows through `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml` → `PathlandSession.renderHtml`.
- The golden harness only compares fragments; there is no document-head cross-renderer fixture.
- Spec already says canonical/robots/sitemap are host-owned, not protocol fields (`spec/OPCODE.md:534`).

---

## 1. Rust renderer: `DocumentMeta` option + SEO head

New files:
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/document.rs`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/structured_data.rs`

`DocumentMeta` (builder-style, pure value, no renderer state):

```rust
pub struct DocumentMeta {
    title: Option<String>,          // fallback; META TITLE wins
    description: Option<String>,    // fallback; META DESCRIPTION wins
    canonical_url: Option<String>,
    site_name: Option<String>,
    image_url: Option<String>,
    og_type: Option<String>,        // default "website"
    twitter_card: Option<String>,   // default summary / summary_large_image
    twitter_site: Option<String>,
    open_graph: bool,
    twitter: bool,
    structured_data: bool,
}
```

Public API additions in `lib.rs`:
- `render_document_with_meta(opcodes, strings, root, &DocumentMeta)`
- `render_document_linked_with_meta(opcodes, strings, root, css_base, &DocumentMeta)`
- Existing methods delegate with `DocumentMeta::none()` so current output/fixtures stay unchanged.

Head emission:
- Effective title/description: `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` value first, then `DocumentMeta` fallback.
- Canonical: `<link rel="canonical" href="...">` when `canonical_url` is present.
- OG when enabled: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type`, `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:image`, `og:locale`.
- Twitter when enabled: `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:site`.
- `og:image` / `twitter:image`: explicit `image_url`, else the first `IMAGE` source in the tree; resolve root-relative paths against the canonical origin when possible.
- All attribute values use the existing HTML escaper.

JSON-LD (`structured_data.rs`):
- Emit only when `structured_data` is enabled and there is something meaningful to describe.
- Build a deterministic `@graph`:
  - `WebPage`: `name`, `description`, `url`, `inLanguage`.
  - One `Article` per `ROLE_ARTICLE` node (document order): `headline` = first heading descendant, `description` = first paragraph descendant, `image` = first `IMAGE` source, `mainEntityOfPage` = canonical, `inLanguage`.
- Fixed key order so Rust and Java can be byte-identical.
- JSON escaping must HTML-safe-escape `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028/U+2029 and normal JSON control characters so app text cannot break out of `<script type="application/ld+json">`.

Tests in the Rust crate:
- canonical/OG/Twitter exact head output
- fallback precedence (`META` wins over `DocumentMeta`)
- JSON-LD WebPage + Article extraction
- script-breakout escaping
- no `DocumentMeta` → byte-identical legacy head

## 2. C ABI parity

In `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/capi.rs`:
- Add `#[repr(C)] PathlandHtmlMeta` with nullable `*const c_char` fields + `u8` enable flags.
- Add `pathland_html_render_with_meta(batch, len, root, css_base, meta, debug)`.
- Keep existing functions unchanged.
- Add C-ABI tests for null meta and populated meta.

## 3. Java renderer parity

New files under `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/`:
- `DocumentMeta.java`
- `StructuredData.java` (or add JSON helpers to `Format.java`)

`HtmlRenderer` additions:
- `render(frame, root, DocumentMeta)`
- `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase, DocumentMeta)`
- `renderLinkedDebug(...)`, `renderDebug(...)` overloads
- Existing methods delegate to `DocumentMeta.none()`
- Refactor `renderDocument` to accept `DocumentMeta` and reuse the same tag construction order as Rust.

Tests:
- `HtmlRendererTest` / new `DocumentMetaTest.kt`:
  - title/meta/landmark assertions for both inline and linked docs
  - canonical/OG/Twitter
  - JSON-LD WebPage + Article
  - escaping/script-breakout

## 4. App-driven per-route metadata in server-core

New types in `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/`:
- `PageMetadata` — neutral transport-agnostic metadata value:
  - nullable `title`, `description`, `canonicalUrl`, `siteName`, `imageUrl`, `ogType`, `twitterCard`, `twitterSite`
  - nullable `Boolean` flags for openGraph/twitter/structuredData
  - `overlay(base)` merge helper
- `PageMetadataRequest` — `route`, `canonicalUrl`, `mountPath`.

`PathlandApp` (`PathlandApp.java`):
- Add a default method, preserving functional-interface compatibility:

```java
default PageMetadata pageMetadata(PageMetadataRequest request) {
    return PageMetadata.empty();
}
```

This is the route-aware hook: the app sees the active, mount-stripped route during SSR and can return route-specific canonical/OG type/image/etc.

`PathlandRegistry`:
- Add `renderHtml(String route, String windowId, PageMetadata hostDefaults)`.
- Existing overloads delegate with `PageMetadata.empty()`.
- Flow:
  1. Build `PageMetadataRequest(stripRoute(route), canonicalUrl, mountPath)`.
  2. Call `app.pageMetadata(request)`.
  3. Merge host defaults ← app metadata (app wins).
  4. Convert to renderer `DocumentMeta` and pass into `PathlandSession`.
- No protocol/session-state change; this is SSR-only metadata, consistent with renderer statelessness.

`PathlandSession`:
- Add `renderHtml(boolean serviceWorker, boolean ssrScoped, DocumentMeta meta)`.
- Existing methods delegate with `DocumentMeta.none()`.

## 5. Starter integration

### Spring Boot
- `PathlandIndexController`:
  - Build canonical from the request URL without query string (`request.getRequestURL()`, not `wID`/query).
  - Build host-default `PageMetadata` from config.
  - Pass it to `registry.renderHtml(route, wid, metadata)`.
- Config keys with safe defaults:
  - `pathland.seo.enabled=true`
  - `pathland.seo.structured-data=true`
  - `pathland.seo.site-name=`
  - `pathland.seo.image=`
  - `pathland.seo.og-type=website`
  - `pathland.seo.twitter-card=`
  - `pathland.seo.twitter-site=`

### Quarkus
- `IndexResource`:
  - Inject `@Context UriInfo` into `index`/`deep`/`render`.
  - Canonical = request URI with query removed.
  - Same `pathland.seo.*` config keys via `@ConfigProperty`.
  - Pass `PageMetadata` to the registry.

### Demos
- Implement `pageMetadata(...)` in the demo `PathlandApp`s (Spring and Quarkus).
  - Example: default website metadata; `/kotlin` route-specific description/OG type.
  - The player route can stay `og:type=website`; article-like routes can return `article`.
- Add demo `application.properties` SEO defaults (site name, optional image/twitter handle).

## 6. Golden conformance + docs

- Extend `pathland-html-golden`:
  - Add a `document_meta` scenario containing WebPage content + an `ROLE_ARTICLE` subtree (heading, paragraph, image).
  - Emit `document_meta.plpl` + `document_meta.document.html` using `render_document_with_meta`.
  - Update `check`/`emit` so the document fixture is guarded.
- Add a Java `DocumentGoldenConformanceTest` comparing the Java renderer against `document_meta.document.html` byte-for-byte.
- TypeScript conformance can ignore `.document.html` (head is not hydrated by the DOM client); no TS renderer change needed.
- Update `status.md` in mandatory places:
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`
  - `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`
  - `lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md`
  - Spring Boot / Quarkus / demo statuses as applicable
- Add a short note to the renderer docs/README: SEO head is host/renderer metadata, not protocol. Optionally add one clarifying sentence in `spec/OPCODE.md` near the window-metadata section; no ID changes.

## 7. Test plan

Rust:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden`
- `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit` (once) then commit fixtures
- `cargo test` workspace

Java:
- `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-server-core,pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-quarkus -am test`
- `mvn install` for the full reactor

JS:
- `cd lib/typescript && npm test` (existing fragment conformance must remain green)

Manual:
- Run Spring and Quarkus demos, `curl -s http://localhost:.../` and verify:
  - `<title>`, description, `<html lang>`
  - canonical link
  - OG/Twitter tags
  - `<script type="application/ld+json">` containing WebPage/Article
  - `<main>`, `<nav>`, heading hierarchy
- Verify a route with app-specific metadata (e.g. `/kotlin`) gets its route-defined values on the first response.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Updating canonical/OG tags during client-side SPA navigation after the initial SSR (title/description already update over `META`; canonical/OG would need a new mechanism).
- Sitemap/robots changes — already host-owned and existing.
- Adding canonical/OG fields to `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` — intentionally avoided to keep web-only artifacts out of the protocol.
- Richer structured data (BreadcrumbList, Organization, ImageObject, per-article URLs) beyond the agreed WebPage + Article scope.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset of
  the property catalog (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding,
  corner radius, opacity, tint, border/shadow color, width/height). Compound
  accumulators that need concrete numbers (e.g. `BORDER_WIDTH`'s px suffix,
  shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.

- **Sequence gap detection** (`transport.ts`, spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap
  detection): each guest → host batch carries a per-stream monotonic `sequence`.
  The client baselines on the first batch and, when a batch's sequence breaks the
  chain (a batch was lost while the socket stayed open), **skips the gapped
  batch** and requests a full snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), then re-baselines.
  Host → guest heartbeat (`PONG`) batches are excluded; the baseline resets on
  every (re)connect. Tests cover contiguous runs (no resync), a gap (resync +
  skip), `PONG` exclusion, and re-baselining after a gap.
- **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**:
  mirrors the Rust SSR — `grid-template-columns`/`grid-template-rows` from the
  `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/
  LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`; never a pixel
  width/height), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/
  `adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/`minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, precedence over the
  count), `gap` from `SPACING`, greedy scroll
  (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`), and **per-cell grid
  alignment** — grid cells are wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose
  `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell else the
  grid `ALIGNMENT` position (`placedChild` + `applyLayout`, the ZStack mirror).
  **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) renders as a transparent `display:contents` element; its
  cell shells get explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement (short rows leave
  trailing columns empty). `SCROLL` and `WHEEL` events are wired to
  document-level listeners gated by the listener bits. A runtime-inserted extra
  `SCROLLVIEW` child is a minor residual (SSR renders only the first child).
- **Canonical keyCode table**: `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` use the DOM `event.keyCode`
  convention; the renderer-shared canonical set lives in the conformance
  vectors (grant WP2) — cross-check on landing.
- **Visual tokens** (`PICKER_STYLE`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`,
  `COLOR_MULTIPLY`) are applied as `data-*` attributes; their *visual* variety is
  renderer-styling-owned (Tailwind/theme), not the protocol's job.
